literature.headline_zh: 猴痘病毒（Mpox病毒）本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期猴痘病毒（Mpox病毒）研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 分支簇I 猴痘 的汇总再生数(R)从1970-2017年的0.71(95% CI 0.26至1.17)上升至2023年后亚分支簇Ib/Ia的1.23(1.12-1.33)。分支簇II 猴痘 在2017-2021年间的R为1.11(0.90-1.32),而在2022-2023年亚分支簇IIb则升至2.66(2.31-3.00)。实证模型研究估计,行为改变与疫苗接种 共同使2022年亚分支簇IIb 暴发 期间的猴痘 病例减少了55%(95% CI 37至73),但效应规模在不同环境中存在差异。 [10.1136/bmjgh-2025-022252]

2024年共报告2,803例猴痘病毒感染病例,其中包括1例与旅行相关的Ib分支病例;2025年共报告2,519例病例,其中包括10例Ib分支病例。2025年9–10月报告的病例数是2024年同期的两倍,但截至2025年12月底,病例数已回落至背景水平。在860名信息完整的患者中,未接种疫苗者的住院风险是完全接种疫苗者的9.73倍(在控制年龄组和HIV感染状况后)。 [10.15585/mmwr.mm7532a1]
该检测方法在线性度、分析灵敏度(检测限在各靶标间为6.7至9.6拷贝/反应)以及在分支水平区分和定量猴痘病毒的特异性方面表现优异。 [10.1099/acmi.0.001041.v3]
整体‘一体化健康’对齐程度有限,无任何疾病×文件类型×目标组合的对齐率超过39%。文件类型差异最为显著:在协调与暴发应对方面,机构技术指导文件的对齐率分别比《联邦公报》文件高13至30个百分点(p值均<0.001)。 [10.20944/preprints202608.1404.v1]
猴痘与行为和社会因素相关,影响特定人群,亟需有效的预防措施及公共政策。 [10.47820/recima21.v7i8.8836]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: The pooled reproduction number (R) for clade I mpox increased from 0.71 (95% CI 0.26 to 1.17) during 1970-2017 to 1.23 (1.12-1.33) for subclades Ib/Ia after 2023. For clade II mpox, R was 1.11 (0.90-1.32) during 2017-2021 and rose to 2.66 (2.31-3.00) for subclade IIb in 2022-2023. [10.1136/bmjgh-2025-022252]
The pooled prevalence of mpox among MSM was estimated at 2.30% [95% confidence interval (CI): 1.29–3.57%]. [10.1186/s40249-026-01493-y]

In 2024, 2,803 MPXV cases were reported, including one travel-associated clade Ib case, while in 2025, 2,519 cases were reported, including 10 clade Ib cases. Cases in September–October 2025 were double those in the same period in 2024 but returned to background levels by December 2025. [10.15585/mmwr.mm7532a1]

The assay demonstrated strong linearity, analytical sensitivity (limits of detection ranged from 6.7 to 9.6 copies per reaction across targets) and specificity in distinguishing and quantifying MPXV by clade. [10.1099/acmi.0.001041.v3]

The pooled positivity rate of mpox virus DNA was 76.7% (95% confidence interval [CI], 27.9%–96.6%) in saliva and 69.7% (95% CI, 40.1%–88.8%) in OPSs. The median shedding durations were 19 and 21 d for saliva and OPSs, respectively. [10.1177/23800844261470373]
literature.trend_or_risk_en: The direction of this week's research is defined by the clinical, epidemiological, ecological, diagnostic and molecular topics actually represented by the eligible publications.
literature.brief_en: This literature brief prioritizes papers published in the active reporting window and ranks them by relevance, evidence availability, study quality, recency, and independent-source convergence. Detailed study-specific evidence is retained in the article cards below.
brief_items_zh: 本期猴痘病毒(Mpox病毒)研究集中呈现以下进展。

分支簇I 猴痘 的汇总再生数(R)从1970-2017年的0.71(95% CI 0.26至1.17)上升至2023年后亚分支簇Ib/Ia的1.23(1.12-1.33)。分支簇II 猴痘 在2017-2021年间的R为1.11(0.90-1.32),而在2022-2023年亚分支簇IIb则升至2.66(2.31-3.00)。实证模型研究估计,行为改变与疫苗接种 共同使2022年亚分支簇IIb 暴发 期间的猴痘 病例减少了55%(95% CI 37至73),但效应规模在不同环境中存在差异。
2024年共报告2,803例猴痘病毒感染病例,其中包括1例与旅行相关的Ib分支病例;2025年共报告2,519例病例,其中包括10例Ib分支病例。2025年9–10月报告的病例数是2024年同期的两倍,但截至2025年12月底,病例数已回落至背景水平。在860名信息完整的患者中,未接种疫苗者的住院风险是完全接种疫苗者的9.73倍(在控制年龄组和HIV感染状况后)。
该检测方法在线性度、分析灵敏度(检测限在各靶标间为6.7至9.6拷贝/反应)以及在分支水平区分和定量猴痘病毒的特异性方面表现优异。 [10.1099/acmi.0.001041.v3]。
整体‘一体化健康’对齐程度有限,无任何疾病×文件类型×目标组合的对齐率超过39%。文件类型差异最为显著:在协调与暴发应对方面,机构技术指导文件的对齐率分别比《联邦公报》文件高13至30个百分点(p值均<0.001)。

news.headline_zh: 猴痘病毒（Mpox病毒）本期公共卫生新闻动态
news.lead_zh: 本期猴痘病毒（Mpox病毒）新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: CDC提供了猴痘病毒的临床概述,特别强调了I型和II型猴痘病毒分支的差异。文件指出,两种分支的传播、治疗和预防方法相似,但其病死率和传播模式可能存在差异。该文件还为医护人员提供了临床检测、诊断和预防的指导。 [news-6361bcd77e6eb0eb]
美国疾病控制与预防中心(CDC)报告称,基于对三名在感染状态下乘机进入或在美国境内飞行的感染者的调查,I支系猴痘病毒(MPXV)在商业航空旅行期间的传播风险极低。 [news-9d171ac0fae55320]
CDC研究显示猴痘可能正在美国成为常驻病原体。该结论为CDC基于研究结果的确认性陈述。 [news-d9b3c522df58348c]
UNICEF报告称,几内亚比绍46例疑似猴痘病例中有23例为15岁以下儿童,表明在最年幼且最脆弱的人群中可能存在隐性传播传播。该暴发是该国首次记录的猴痘暴发。 [news-c9e44fd7cc6feaf4]
科罗拉多州报告 猴痘 感染夏季激增,自 7 月下旬起新增 7 例,今年累计 18 例(2025 年全年为 21 例)。丹佛公共卫生与环境部门自 6 月 1 日起已报告 6 例。病例间无已知关联或共同暴露史,但可能在时间上形成聚集。 [news-cbe582f0e1a4aae8]
news.trend_or_risk_zh: 风险判断仅依据入选来源已经确认的信息，不把媒体推测升级为官方结论。
news.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following Mpox virus news developments.
key_findings_en: The CDC provides a clinical overview of the monkeypox virus, specifically highlighting the differences between clade I and clade II MPXV. It notes that both clades can be spread, treated, and prevented similarly, but their case-fatality rates and transmission patterns may vary. [news-6361bcd77e6eb0eb]

The CDC reported that the transmission risk for clade I monkeypox virus (MPXV) during commercial air travel appears to be very low, based on investigations involving three infected travelers who flew into or within the United States while infectious. [news-9d171ac0fae55320]

The CDC study suggests that mpox is likely becoming endemic in the United States. This is a reported statement by the CDC, and the status is confirmed based on the study's findings. [news-d9b3c522df58348c]

UNICEF reported that 23 of Guinea-Bissau's 46 suspected mpox cases are children under 15, indicating a potential silent transmission among the youngest and most vulnerable population. The outbreak is the country's first recorded mpox outbreak. [news-c9e44fd7cc6feaf4]

A summer surge in Mpox infections has been reported in Colorado, with seven cases since late July and 18 cases recorded this year compared to 21 in all of 2025. The Denver Department of Public Health and Environment has seen six cases since June 1. [news-cbe582f0e1a4aae8]

papers.title: Dynamics of global mpox epidemics, 1970-2025: a systematic review and meta-analysis of evolving transmissibility and intervention effects.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The 2022 global mpox epidemic declined before modified Vaccinia Ankara-Bavarian Nordic (MVA-BN) vaccines were widely deployed, contributing to the perception that transmission was self-limiting within a small high-risk population. This may have delayed global vaccine allocation and weakened responses to the resurgence that has disproportionately affected Africa since 2024. The reasons for the 2022 decline remain uncertain, and prior studies have reported widely divergent estimates of vaccination impact. We systematically reviewed and meta-analysed the evolving transmissibility of mpox clades and the effects of interventions. METHODS: We searched GenBank, PubMed and Embase through 18 May 2025, for mpox virus sequences, reproduction number (R) estimates and modelling studies evaluating intervention effectiveness. Two reviewers independently assessed eligibility, extracted data and evaluated risk of bias using a validated tool. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed. RESULTS: Fifty-two studies reporting R estimates and 40 studies evaluating intervention effectiveness met eligibility criteria. For clade I mpox, pooled R increased from 0.71 (95% CI 0.26 to 1.17) during 1970-2017 to 1.23 (1.12-1.33) for subclades Ib/Ia after 2023 (p=0.0303). For clade II mpox, pooled R was 1.11 (0.90-1.32) during 2017-2021 and increased to 2.66 (2.31-3.00) for subclade IIb in 2022-2023 (p<0.0001). During the 2022 subclade IIb outbreak, empirical modelling studies estimated that behaviour change and vaccination together were associated with a substantial reduction in mpox cases (55%, 95% CI 37 to 73; I2=81.2%), although effect sizes varied across settings according to the extent of behaviour change and the timing and coverage of vaccine rollout. CONCLUSIONS: Behaviour change and vaccination likely played important roles in the decline of the 2022 mpox epidemic in many studied settings. Given the stepwise increase in human-to-human transmissibility associated with the emergence of new subclades, effective mpox epidemic control requires proactive, rapid and equitable vaccine rollout supported by culturally tailored risk communication. PROSPERO REGISTRATION NUMBER: CRD420250653072.

This may have delayed global vaccine allocation and weakened responses to the resurgence that has disproportionately affected Africa since 2024. The reasons for the 2022 decline remain uncertain, and prior studies have reported widely divergent estimates of vaccination impact. We systematically reviewed and meta-analysed the evolving transmissibility of mpox clades and the effects of interventions. Methods We searched GenBank, PubMed and Embase through 18 May 2025, for mpox virus sequences, reproduction number (R) estimates and modelling studies evaluating intervention effectiveness. Two reviewers independently assessed eligibility, extracted data and evaluated risk of bias using a validated tool. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed. Results Fifty-two studies reporting R estimates and 40 studies evaluating intervention effectiveness met eligibility criteria. For clade I mpox, pooled R increased from 0.71 (95% CI 0.26 to 1.17) during 1970-2017 to 1.23 (1.12-1.33) for subclades Ib/Ia after 2023 (p=0.0303). For clade II mpox, pooled R was 1.11 (0.90-1.32) during 2017-2021 and increased to 2.66 (2.31-3.00) for subclade IIb in 2022-2023 (p 2 =81.2%), although effect sizes varied across settings according to the extent of behaviour change and the timing and coverage of vaccine rollout. Conclusions Behaviour change and vaccination likely played important roles in the decline of the 2022 mpox epidemic in many studied settings. Given the stepwise increase in human-to-human transmissibility associated with the emergence of new subclades, effective mpox epidemic control requires proactive, rapid and equitable vaccine rollout supported by culturally tailored risk communication. Prospero registration number CRD420250653072.

This may have delayed global vaccine allocation and weakened responses to the resurgence that has disproportionately affected Africa since 2024. The reasons for the 2022 decline remain uncertain, and prior studies have reported widely divergent estimates of vaccination impact. We systematically reviewed and meta-analysed the evolving transmissibility of mpox clades and the effects of interventions. METHODS: We searched GenBank, PubMed and Embase through 18 May 2025, for mpox virus sequences, reproduction number (R) estimates and modelling studies evaluating intervention effectiveness. Two reviewers independently assessed eligibility, extracted data and evaluated risk of bias using a validated tool. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed. RESULTS: Fifty-two studies reporting R estimates and 40 studies evaluating intervention effectiveness met eligibility criteria. For clade I mpox, pooled R increased from 0.71 (95% CI 0.26 to 1.17) during 1970-2017 to 1.23 (1.12-1.33) for subclades Ib/Ia after 2023 (p=0.0303). For clade II mpox, pooled R was 1.11 (0.90-1.32) during 2017-2021 and increased to 2.66 (2.31-3.00) for subclade IIb in 2022-2023 (p<0.0001). During the 2022 subclade IIb outbreak, empirical modelling studies estimated that behaviour change and vaccination together were associated with a substantial reduction in mpox cases (55%, 95% CI 37 to 73; I2=81.2%), although effect sizes varied across settings according to the extent of behaviour change and the timing and coverage of vaccine rollout. Given the stepwise increase in human-to-human transmissibility associated with the emergence of new subclades, effective mpox epidemic control requires proactive, rapid and equitable vaccine rollout supported by culturally tailored risk communication. papers.title_original: Dynamics of global mpox epidemics, 1970-2025: a systematic review and meta-analysis of evolving transmissibility and intervention effects.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the dynamics of global mpox epidemics from 1970 to 2025, examining the evolving transmissibility of mpox clades and the effects of interventions. The central question is whether behavior change and vaccination have played significant roles in controlling mpox outbreaks, particularly during the 2022 epidemic and subsequent resurgence in Africa.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The evidence base includes mpox virus sequences, reproduction number (R) estimates, and modeling studies evaluating intervention effectiveness. The review searched GenBank, PubMed, and Embase through 18 May 2025. Two reviewers independently assessed eligibility, extracted data, and evaluated risk of bias using a validated tool. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed to synthesize findings.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The pooled reproduction number (R) for clade I mpox increased from 0.71 (95% CI 0.26 to 1.17) during 1970-2017 to 1.23 (1.12-1.33) for subclades Ib/Ia after 2023. For clade II mpox, R was 1.11 (0.90-1.32) during 2017-2021 and rose to 2.66 (2.31-3.00) for subclade IIb in 2022-2023. Empirical modeling studies estimated that behavior change and vaccination together reduced mpox cases by 55% (95% CI 37 to 73) during the 2022 subclade IIb outbreak, though effect sizes varied by setting.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The reasons for the 2022 decline in mpox cases remain uncertain, with prior studies reporting widely divergent estimates of vaccination impact. The evidence also highlights heterogeneity in intervention effectiveness, influenced by the extent of behavior change and the timing and coverage of vaccine rollout. There is a lack of consensus on the exact mechanisms driving the increased transmissibility of new subclades.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Effective mpox epidemic control requires proactive, rapid, and equitable vaccine rollout, supported by culturally tailored risk communication. The review emphasizes the need for further research on the mechanisms of increased transmissibility in new subclades and the optimization of intervention strategies across different settings.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis investigate the dynamics of global mpox epidemics from 1970 to 2025, focusing on the evolving transmissibility of mpox clades and the impact of interventions. The review highlights a significant increase in the reproduction number (R) for clade IIb mpox, particularly in 2022-2023, compared to earlier periods. It also reports that behavior change and vaccination were associated with a substantial reduction in mpox cases during the 2022 outbreak, though effect sizes varied by setting. The findings underscore the importance of rapid and equitable vaccine distribution, supported by culturally appropriate risk communication, to control mpox epidemics. The review identifies uncertainties in the reasons for the 2022 decline and calls for further research on the mechanisms of increased transmissibility in new subclades.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述关注1970年至2025年全球猴痘疫情的动态,研究猴痘分支的传播力变化以及干预措施的效果。核心问题是行为改变和疫苗接种是否在控制猴痘疫情,尤其是在2022年疫情及随后非洲的疫情反弹中发挥了重要作用。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 证据基础包括猴痘病毒序列、繁殖数(R)估计值以及评估干预效果的建模研究。本综述于2025年5月18日通过GenBank、PubMed和Embase进行检索。两名评审员独立评估了资格、提取数据并使用经过验证的工具评估偏倚风险。进行了随机效应荟萃分析以综合研究结果。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 分支簇I 猴痘 的汇总再生数(R)从1970-2017年的0.71(95% CI 0.26至1.17)上升至2023年后亚分支簇Ib/Ia的1.23(1.12-1.33)。分支簇II 猴痘 在2017-2021年间的R为1.11(0.90-1.32),而在2022-2023年亚分支簇IIb则升至2.66(2.31-3.00)。实证模型研究估计,行为改变与疫苗接种 共同使2022年亚分支簇IIb 暴发 期间的猴痘 病例减少了55%(95% CI 37至73),但效应规模在不同环境中存在差异。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 2022年猴痘病例下降的原因仍不确定,先前研究对疫苗接种的影响估计差异很大。证据还突出了干预效果的异质性,这受到行为改变程度以及疫苗部署的时间和覆盖范围的影响。对于新亚分支传播力增加的确切机制尚无共识。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 有效的猴痘疫情控制需要由文化定制的风险沟通支持的主动、快速和公平的疫苗部署。本综述强调需要进一步研究新亚分支传播力增加的机制以及在不同环境中优化干预策略。

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:2022年全球猴痘疫情在改良型牛痘病毒-巴伐利亚北(MVA-BN)疫苗广泛部署之前出现下降,这导致人们认为传播在小规模高风险人群中具有自限性。这可能延迟了全球疫苗的分配,并削弱了对自2024年以来主要影响非洲的疫情反弹的应对。2022年疫情下降的原因仍不确定,先前研究对疫苗接种的影响估计差异很大。我们系统综述并荟萃分析了猴痘分支的传播力变化以及干预措施的效果。方法:我们于2025年5月18日通过GenBank、PubMed和Embase检索了猴痘病毒序列、繁殖数(R)估计值和评估干预效果的建模研究。两名评审员独立评估了资格、提取数据并使用经过验证的工具评估偏倚风险。进行了随机效应荟萃分析。结果:有52项研究报告了R估计值,40项研究评估了干预效果,符合纳入标准。对于I型猴痘分支,合并后的R值从1970年至2017年的0.71(95% CI 0.26至1.17)上升至2023年后Ib/Ia亚分支的1.23(1.12-1.33)(p=0.0303)。对于II型猴痘分支,合并后的R值在2017年至2021年为1.11(0.90-1.32),而在2022年至2023年的IIb亚分支中上升至2.66(2.31-3.00)(p<0.0001)。在2022年IIb亚分支暴发期间,实证建模研究估计,行为改变和疫苗接种共同作用导致猴痘病例显著减少(55%,95% CI 37至73;I2=81.2%),尽管不同环境下的效应大小因行为改变的程度以及疫苗部署的时间和覆盖范围而有所不同。结论:在许多研究环境中,行为改变和疫苗接种可能在2022年猴痘疫情下降中发挥了重要作用。鉴于新亚分支出现与人传人传播力逐步增加相关,有效的猴痘疫情控制需要由文化定制的风险沟通支持的主动、快速和公平的疫苗部署。PROSPERO注册号:CRD420250653072。

papers.title: Prevalence of mpox infection among men who have sex with men: a systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Mpox has been twice declared as public health emergency of international concern by World Health Organization. The 2022–2024 global outbreak has been primarily driven by sexual transmission within men who have sex with men (MSM) networks, predominantly involving Clade IIb, with a subsequent surge of Clade Ib in early 2024. MSM account for a large proportion of confirmed mpox cases. This review aimed to estimate the prevalence of mpox infection among MSM populations. Methods We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI) and Wanfang Data for studies published in English or Chinese from inception to 16 December 2024. Eligible studies reported mpox cases among MSM with confirmed diagnosis (laboratory or self-reported) during the outbreak period. Reviews, case reports, and studies without case numbers were excluded. American Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality and Newcastle-Ottawa Scale were adopted for quality assessment. Fixed-effects or random-effects meta-analysis was performed to estimate the pooled prevalence of mpox among MSM. Heterogeneity was measured using Cochran's Q test and I 2 statistics. Meta regression analysis was performed to discover the potential source of the heterogeneity. Funnel plot, Egger's regression test and Begg's rank correlation test were conducted to evaluate the publication bias. Sensitivity analyses were performed by leave-one-out analysis and by stratified validation. Results From 1606 retrieved studies, 28 studies were eligible and included, containing a total of 46,598 MSM participants and 1274 mpox cases from 15 countries. The pooled mpox prevalence among MSM population was 2.30% [95% confidence interval ( CI ): 1.29–3.57%]. Meta-regression identified continent as the most significant moderator, with prevalence in South America (9.58, 95% CI : 2.71–20.01%) being significantly higher than in Asia (1.14, 95% CI : 0.56–1.90%) ( P = 0.019). Sampling method also contributed to the heterogeneity, whereas no statistically significant difference was observed in mpox prevalence among high-risk MSM, asymptomatic MSM, comparing to the general MSM populations respectively. Conclusions This study confirms a significant but highly heterogeneous burden of mpox among MSM worldwide. The findings suggest that the observed prevalence is shaped more by regional epidemiological contexts and study methodologies, which emphasizes the necessity for geographically prioritized interventions and standardizing surveillance to enable accurate risk assessment and guide resource allocation in future outbreaks.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review aimed to estimate the prevalence of mpox infection among men who have sex with men (MSM) populations globally, focusing on the role of sexual transmission and the impact of different clades of the mpox virus.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The evidence base included 28 studies retrieved from PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), and Wanfang Data, covering studies published in English or Chinese from inception to 16 December 2024. The review used fixed-effects or random-effects meta-analysis to estimate pooled prevalence, with heterogeneity assessed using Cochran's Q test and I 2 statistics. Meta-regression was conducted to identify potential sources of heterogeneity, and publication bias was evaluated using funnel plots, Egger's regression test, and Begg's rank correlation test. Sensitivity analyses were performed via leave-one-out and stratified validation methods.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The pooled prevalence of mpox among MSM was estimated at 2.30% [95% confidence interval (CI): 1.29–3.57%]. Meta-regression identified continent as the most significant moderator, with South America showing a significantly higher prevalence (9.58, 95% CI: 2.71–20.01%) compared to Asia (1.14, 95% CI: 0.56–1.90%) (P = 0.019). The study concluded that mpox prevalence among MSM is significant but highly heterogeneous, influenced by regional epidemiological contexts and study methodologies.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review noted that sampling methods contributed to heterogeneity, but no statistically significant difference in prevalence was observed among high-risk MSM, asymptomatic MSM, or general MSM populations. There is a lack of clarity on the exact mechanisms driving the surge in Clade Ib cases in early 2024, and the study did not provide detailed insights into the biological or ecological factors behind the regional variations in prevalence.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The findings highlight the need for geographically prioritized interventions and standardized surveillance to enable accurate risk assessment and guide resource allocation in future outbreaks. The review suggests that future research should focus on understanding the epidemiological and ecological factors contributing to the regional variations in mpox prevalence among MSM, as well as the role of different clades in transmission dynamics.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to estimate the prevalence of mpox infection among men who have sex with men (MSM) populations globally. The pooled prevalence of mpox among MSM was found to be 2.30% [95% CI: 1.29–3.57%], with significant regional variation, particularly between South America and Asia. Meta-regression identified continent as the most significant moderator, and the study concluded that the observed heterogeneity is shaped by regional epidemiological contexts and study methodologies. The findings emphasize the importance of geographically targeted interventions and standardized surveillance to improve risk assessment and resource allocation in future outbreaks. However, the review noted gaps in understanding the mechanisms behind the surge in Clade Ib cases and the role of sampling methods in influencing results.

papers.title: Mpox Airborne Transmission: A Systematic Review.
papers.abstract: Since May 2022, mpox has been reported across multiple nonendemic regions, with concurrent outbreaks in diverse geographic settings, raising concerns about broader international spread. However, evidence regarding the risk of airborne transmission remains limited. We conducted a systematic review to evaluate the risk of airborne transmission and the presence of viable viruses in air samples. PubMed, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched for studies published in English, including environmental studies, case reports, cross-sectional studies, and cohort studies. Data extraction included study characteristics (authors, year, design, and setting), sample size, diagnostic methods, participant characteristics, follow-up, type of respiratory particles assessed (droplets and/or aerosols), and key findings. Of 286 records identified, four studies met the inclusion criteria. All were environmental studies published between 2022 and 2023. MPXV DNA was detected in surface and air samples, with cycle threshold (Ct) values ranging from < 30 to < 45. However, none of the studies demonstrated consistent viral viability in aerosols or droplets sufficient to support airborne transmission. Overall, the available evidence is limited and does not support a clear risk of airborne infection. Further well-designed studies in human settings are needed to clarify the potential for mpox transmission through respiratory routes. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO: CRD42023391123.

papers.title: Saliva and Oropharyngeal Swabs as Screening Tools for Mpox: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
papers.abstract: Objectives: The global mpox outbreak that began in 2020 was declared a public health emergency of international concern in 2024. However, there is limited scientific evidence regarding the use of salivary and/or oropharyngeal swab samples to detect the virus. In this review, we systematically examined existing literature to evaluate the potential of saliva and/or oropharyngeal swab samples as screening tools for mpox detection. Methods: The final analysis included 15 articles comprising 2,610 participants, including mpox-infected individuals (polymerase chain reaction confirmed) whose saliva and/or oropharyngeal samples (OPSs) tested positive for the virus. After a quality assessment, a random-effects model with logit transformation was used to pool the positivity rates. Results: The pooled positivity rate of mpox virus DNA was 76.7% (95% confidence interval [CI], 27.9%–96.6%) in saliva and 69.7% (95% CI, 40.1%–88.8%) in OPSs. The high heterogeneity between the studies (I 2 = 99.5%) for both specimen types was addressed through sensitivity analyses. The median shedding durations were 19 and 21 d for saliva and OPSs, respectively. Conclusions: The high positivity rates and sustained shedding in saliva and OPSs indicate that these methods can serve as noninvasive, adjunct, early-phase alternatives for rapid mpox detection, supporting enhanced surveillance, outbreak monitoring, and global public health preparedness. Knowledge Transfer Statement: The findings of this systematic review are directly relevant to clinicians, dental surgeons, and infection control specialists in understanding the diagnostic value of saliva and oropharyngeal samples for mpox. This knowledge can aid in screening, infection control, and patient management within health care settings.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis assesses the diagnostic utility of saliva and oropharyngeal swab samples for mpox detection. The review includes 15 studies with 2,610 participants, focusing on polymerase chain reaction-confirmed mpox cases. Pooled positivity rates for saliva and oropharyngeal swabs were 76.7% (95% CI, 27.9%–96.6%) and 69.7% (95% CI, 40.1%–88.8%), respectively, with median shedding durations of 19 and 21 days. The findings are relevant for clinicians, dental surgeons, and infection control specialists in improving diagnostic practices and infection control measures in healthcare settings.

papers.title: Emerging infectious diseases (Mpox, Nipah, and Andes): A narrative review of transmission, environmental survival, and disinfection
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Mpox, Nipah virus, and Andes virus are emerging infectious diseases that cause outbreaks associated with nosocomial transmission. METHODS: This narrative review summarizes the Mpox, Nipah virus, and Andes virus epidemiology, clinical manifestations, diagnosis, and treatment with a focus on environmental survival, susceptibility to antiseptics and disinfectants, and infection prevention. RESULTS: Mpox, Nipah virus, and Andes virus all survive in the environment and are capable of indirect transmission. All these viruses are enveloped and susceptible to commonly used antiseptics and surface disinfectants. CONCLUSIONS: Rapid identification of patients with known or suspected infections of these emerging viruses coupled with adherence to infection prevention recommendations will prevent healthcare-associated transmission.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines Monkeypox virus (MPXV), including mpox disease, its clades (clade I, clade II, clade Ib), and associated outbreaks with a focus on nosocomial transmission and infection prevention in healthcare settings.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This narrative review synthesizes epidemiology, clinical features, diagnosis, treatment, environmental survival, susceptibility to antiseptics and disinfectants, and infection prevention strategies for MPXV and related orthopoxviruses.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: MPXV demonstrates environmental survival and indirect transmission potential, and as an enveloped virus, it remains susceptible to commonly used antiseptics and surface disinfectants.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The supplied evidence does not report heterogeneity in environmental survival across MPXV clades, nor does it provide comparative data on disinfectant efficacy specifically stratified by clade or environmental conditions.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Rapid identification of patients with suspected mpox and strict adherence to infection prevention recommendations are critical to preventing healthcare-associated transmission of MPXV.

analysis.summary_en: This narrative review focuses on Monkeypox virus (MPXV), including mpox disease and its clades, emphasizing nosocomial transmission risks and infection control. It synthesizes evidence on MPXV epidemiology, clinical features, diagnosis, treatment, environmental survival, and susceptibility to antiseptics and disinfectants. Key findings confirm that MPXV can survive in the environment and is susceptible to standard disinfectants due to its enveloped structure. The review highlights the importance of rapid patient identification and adherence to infection prevention measures to mitigate healthcare-associated transmission. Evidence gaps include limited data on clade-specific environmental survival and disinfectant efficacy under varied conditions.

analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本综述综合分析了流行病学、临床特征、诊断、治疗、环境生存能力、对消毒剂和防腐剂的敏感性以及猴痘病毒(MPXV)及其相关正痘病毒的感染预防策略。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 猴痘病毒(MPXV)具有环境存活能力,并存在间接传播传播潜力;作为包膜病毒,其对常用消毒剂和表面消毒剂仍然敏感。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 所提供的证据未报告猴痘病毒不同分支在环境存活能力上的异质性,亦未提供按分支或环境条件分层的消毒剂效力对比数据。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 快速识别疑似猴痘患者并严格遵守感染预防建议,对于预防与猴痘病毒相关的医源性传播至关重要。

papers.title: Monkeypox Virus Surveillance — United States, 2024–2025
papers.abstract: Since the onset of a global outbreak of monkeypox virus (MPXV) infections in 2022, cases have declined substantially in the United States; however, ongoing low-level transmission has persisted. To assess trends in cases of MPXV infection in the United States during 2024-2025, investigators analyzed data from the One CDC Data Platform and the National Notifiable Diseases Surveillance System. In 2024, a total of 2,803 cases of MPXV infection were reported in the United States, including one travel-associated clade Ib case. In 2025, a total of 2,519 cases were reported, including 10 clade Ib cases. The number of reported cases of MPXV infection during September-October 2025 was double that during the same period in 2024, although cases returned to background levels by the end of December 2025. Demographic characteristics of patients with MPXV infections, including distributions by sex, race and ethnicity, sexual orientation, lesion location, and age, were similar to those reported in previous years. Among 860 patients with complete information, the odds of hospitalization among those who were unvaccinated were 9.73 times those who were fully vaccinated when controlling for age group and HIV status. Encouraging completion of the recommended 2-dose vaccination series for persons at risk for MPXV exposure, including travelers to specific countries with ongoing clade I or clade II transmission, could reduce the risk for severe illness and hospitalization. Continued routine surveillance remains important to limiting future spread, monitoring changes in viral evolution, and focusing vaccination efforts on affected areas.
papers.journal: MMWR. Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report

papers.title: Clade-specific multiplex digital PCR assay for monkeypox virus detection in spike-in wastewater samples.
papers.abstract: Monkeypox virus (MPXV) is a zoonotic pathogen that has recently caused outbreaks in non-endemic areas. Wastewater-based surveillance is independent of individual testing and offers substantial potential for monitoring population-level disease dynamics of MPXV at the clade level, as clades differ in transmissibility and mortality rate. Here, we report the validation of a four-plex digital PCR assay to detect and quantify the major clades and subclades of MPXV. The assay demonstrated strong linearity, analytical sensitivity (limits of detection ranged from 6.7 to 9.6 copies per reaction across targets) and specificity in distinguishing and quantifying MPXV by clade, which is advantageous for both clinical and wastewater applications.

analysis.summary_en: This study presents a clade-specific multiplex digital PCR assay for detecting and quantifying monkeypox virus (MPXV) in wastewater samples. The research was motivated by the need to monitor MPXV outbreaks in non-endemic areas, as the virus is zoonotic and has recently caused significant public health concerns. The assay was validated using spike-in wastewater samples, showing strong linearity, analytical sensitivity, and specificity in distinguishing and quantifying MPXV by clade. These results highlight the potential of the assay for both clinical and wastewater-based surveillance, offering a valuable tool for understanding MPXV dynamics at the clade level. The study's findings are significant for public health, as they can aid in tracking population-level disease trends. However, the study is limited to spike-in samples, which may not fully reflect real-world conditions, and the evidence is strong due to the assay's demonstrated performance.

elements_zh.methods: 该检测方法在添加猴痘病毒的废水样本中进行了验证,以评估其检测和定量猴痘病毒分支的能力。该方法在线性度、分析灵敏度以及在分支水平区分和定量猴痘病毒的特异性方面表现优异。
elements_zh.main_results: 该检测方法在线性度、分析灵敏度(检测限在各靶标间为6.7至9.6拷贝/反应)以及在分支水平区分和定量猴痘病毒的特异性方面表现优异。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将研究结果解释为证明该检测方法在临床和废水应用中的潜力。其创新之处在于开发了一种猴痘病毒分支特异性多重数字PCR检测方法。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可为基于废水的监测提供依据,用于监测猴痘病毒(MPXV)种群水平疾病动态,这对于理解不同分支间传播能力和抗病毒药物敏感性差异具有重要意义。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅限于添加猴痘病毒的废水样本,可能无法完全代表真实世界条件。然而,该检测方法在线性度、分析灵敏度和特异性方面表现优异,证据强度较高。

papers.title: Dermoscopic Features of Mpox: A Case Series
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Monkeypox (mpox) is a viral infection characterized by polymorphic cutaneous lesions and systemic symptoms, including fever, lymphadenopathy, headache and myalgia. Given its broad differential diagnosis, accurate recognition requires a high level of clinical suspicion; in this context, dermoscopy represents a potentially useful tool to improve diagnostic accuracy. We conducted a retrospective case series of six patients with RT‐PCR–confirmed mpox and dermatologic involvement between July 2022 and July 2025. A total of six patients were included; three (50%) were evaluated in the macular/vesicular phase and three (50%) in the crusted phase. In the macular/vesicular phase, eight lesions were analysed. In the crusted phase, five lesions were analysed. In our series, we observed pinkish‐yellow structureless areas during the macular/vesicular phase. Recognition of these dermoscopic features may increase clinical suspicion and support the diagnosis.

papers.title: Evaluating U.S. Federal Zoonotic Records Against National One Health Goals: A Multi-LLM Assessment Across COVID-19, Mpox, and H5N1
papers.abstract: (1) Background: Zoonotic diseases require coordinated action across human, animal, and environmental health sectors. While substantial research has focused on outbreak prediction, forecasting, and surveillance, less attention has been given to systematically evaluating how One Health principles are reflected in government policy documents. (2) Methods: We developed a multi–large language model (LLM) framework to evaluate 477 U.S. government documents covering COVID-19, mpox, and highly pathogenic avian influenza (H5N1). Agency technical guidance and Federal Register documents were evaluated using a 19-item rubric covering three goals of the U.S. National One Health Framework: coordination and communication, outbreak response, and surveillance. Claude, GPT, and Gemini independently evaluated the documents, with agreement assessed using Fleiss’ κ and independent human validation. (3) Results: One Health alignment was generally limited, with no disease × document-type × goal combination exceeding 39%. Document type showed the clearest differences: agency technical guidance had 13 to 30 percentage-point higher alignment than Federal Register documents for coordination and outbreak response, respectively (both p < 0.001). Differences across diseases were less consistent. After excluding one wording-sensitive rubric item, the three LLMs reached unanimous agreement in 87.1% of document-item evaluations. Human–model agreement (Cohen’s κ = 0.513–0.692) was comparable to human–human agreement (κ = 0.649). (4) Conclusions: Three main findings emerged: document type showed clearer differences in One Health alignment than disease or publication period; clearer and more operational criteria supported more consistent evaluation; and multi-LLM consensus showed strong reproducibility for scalable policy assessment. Together, these findings extend zoonotic-disease research beyond outbreak prediction and surveillance toward systematic evaluation of One Health policy.

papers.abstract_zh: (1) 背景:人兽共患病需要在人类、动物与环境健康部门间开展协调行动。尽管大量研究聚焦于暴发预测、预报与监测,但针对政府政策文件中‘一体化健康’原则体现情况的系统性评估关注较少。(2) 方法:本研究构建多大语言模型(LLM)框架,评估了477份美国政府文件,涵盖COVID-19、猴痘与高致病性禽流感(H5N1)。采用包含19个评分项的评估量表,对美国‘国家一体化健康框架’的三大目标进行评估:协调与沟通、暴发应对与监测。Claude、GPT与Gemini三个模型独立评估文件,采用Fleiss κ系数评估一致性,并由人工进行独立验证。(3) 结果:整体‘一体化健康’对齐程度有限,无任何疾病×文件类型×目标组合的对齐率超过39%。文件类型差异最为显著:在协调与暴发应对方面,机构技术指导文件的对齐率分别比《联邦公报》文件高13至30个百分点(p值均<0.001)。疾病间差异不一致。在排除一项对措辞敏感的评分项后,三个LLM在87.1%的文件-评分项评估中达成一致。人类-模型一致性(Cohen κ=0.513–0.692)与人类-人类一致性(κ=0.649)相当。(4) 结论:研究得出三项主要发现:文件类型在‘一体化健康’对齐程度上较疾病或发布时间更显著;更清晰与可操作的评估标准可提升一致性;多LLM共识在可扩展政策评估中表现出较强的可重复性。这些发现将人兽共患病研究从暴发预测与监测扩展至‘一体化健康’政策的系统性评估。

papers.title: Multiomics profiling of plasma reveals lipid-immune dysregulation and exosome remodeling in mpox and mpox-HIV co-infection.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Monkeypox virus (MPXV) infects diverse human cell types, and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) co-infection is common. The immunometabolic consequences of MPXV infection, and how it may be altered by HIV, remain poorly defined. METHODS: We performed quantitative plasma lipidomics and precise metabolomics in a discovery cohort (n = 81) comprising MPXV-monoinfected (MPLWOH), MPXV-HIV-coinfected (MPLWH), and HIV-monoinfected (PLWH) patients and healthy controls, integrating exosome proteomics, cytokine profiling, and transcriptomics of exosome-treated HepG2 and A549 cells for functional interpretation. An independent validation cohort (n = 65) was used to assess cross-cohort reproducibility. FINDINGS: MPXV infection induced broad lipid remodeling, with elevations in phosphatidylserine (PS) and phosphatidylethanolamine (PE) and reductions in phosphatidylcholine (PC), lysophospholipids, cholesteryl ester (CE), and exosomal lecithin-cholesterol acyltransferase (LCAT) and lipoprotein lipase (LPL). These lipid alterations were correlated with tissue injury markers and inflammatory cytokines. The MPLWH group exhibited more severe metabolic disruption, including marked sulfatide (SL) depletion, lower cholesterol and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-c), and extensive rewiring of lipid-cytokine associations. SL depletion in MPLWH correlated with abundances of COPI-mediated retrograde trafficking proteins in exosomes. Transcriptomic profiling of exosome-treated cells provided functional validation: MPLWOH exosomes induced lipid metabolism and repair-associated epithelial programs, while MPLWH exosomes drove phospholipid remodeling and acute inflammatory and mucosal barrier-stress responses. CONCLUSIONS: MPXV infection reprograms host lipid metabolism and exosome composition, with HIV co-infection amplifying inflammatory, metabolic, and trafficking disruptions. These convergent multi-omics signatures link systemic lipid dysregulation to exosome-mediated immunomodulation and identify potential targets for host-directed interventions. FUNDING: This study was funded by the Major Project of Guangzhou National Laboratory.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the immunometabolic consequences of monkeypox virus (MPXV) infection and the impact of HIV co-infection using multiomics profiling of plasma and exosomes. In a discovery cohort of 81 participants and a validation cohort of 65, MPXV infection was associated with broad lipid remodeling, including elevations in phosphatidylserine and phosphatidylethanolamine and reductions in phosphatidylcholine and cholesteryl ester, alongside decreased exosomal LCAT and LPL. These lipid changes correlated with tissue injury markers and inflammatory cytokines. HIV co-infection exacerbated metabolic disruption, marked by sulfatide depletion, lower cholesterol and HDL-c, and extensive rewiring of lipid-cytokine associations. Functional transcriptomics of exosome-treated cells showed MPXV-monoinfected exosomes induced lipid metabolism and repair programs, while MPXV-HIV-coinfected exosomes drove phospholipid remodeling and inflammatory responses. The authors conclude that MPXV reprograms host lipid metabolism and exosome composition, with HIV amplifying these disruptions, and propose host-directed intervention targets.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究探讨了猴痘病毒(MPXV)感染的免疫代谢后果,以及人类免疫缺陷病毒(HIV)共感染如何改变这些过程,尽管MPXV具有广泛的细胞嗜性且HIV共感染较为常见,但这些过程此前仍未明确。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究在一项发现队列研究中进行了定量血浆脂质组学和代谢组学分析,该队列包括81名参与者,涵盖MPXV单感染、MPXV-HIV共感染、HIV单感染患者以及健康对照组,并使用独立验证队列研究(n = 65)评估结果的可重复性。
elements_zh.methods: 进行了血浆脂质组学和代谢组学分析,并结合外泌体蛋白组学、细胞因子谱分析以及外泌体处理的HepG2和A549细胞的转录组学分析,以功能化解释研究结果。
elements_zh.main_results: MPXV感染导致广泛的脂质重塑,表现为磷脂酰丝氨酸和磷脂酰乙醇胺升高,而磷脂酰胆碱、溶血磷脂、胆固醇酯以及外泌体中的卵磷脂胆固醇乙酰转移酶(LCAT)和脂蛋白脂肪酶(LPL)水平降低,这些变化与组织损伤标志物和炎症细胞因子相关。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,MPXV感染重新编程了宿主的脂质代谢和外泌体组成,HIV共感染则放大了炎症、代谢和运输的紊乱,并识别出将系统性脂质失调与外泌体介导的免疫调节联系起来的一致多组学特征。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明,针对宿主的干预措施可能成为缓解猴痘和猴痘-HIV共感染中免疫代谢失调的潜在靶点,为未来的治疗和诊断策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性包括缺乏纵向采样和体内功能验证,这限制了因果推断和结果的普遍性,因此证据的可信度为中等。

The immunometabolic consequences of MPXV infection, and how it may be altered by HIV, remain poorly defined. METHODS: We performed quantitative plasma lipidomics and precise metabolomics in a discovery cohort (n = 81) comprising MPXV-monoinfected (MPLWOH), MPXV-HIV-coinfected (MPLWH), and HIV-monoinfected (PLWH) patients and healthy controls, integrating exosome proteomics, cytokine profiling, and transcriptomics of exosome-treated HepG2 and A549 cells for functional interpretation. An independent validation cohort (n = 65) was used to assess cross-cohort reproducibility. FINDINGS: MPXV infection induced broad lipid remodeling, with elevations in phosphatidylserine (PS) and phosphatidylethanolamine (PE) and reductions in phosphatidylcholine (PC), lysophospholipids, cholesteryl ester (CE), and exosomal lecithin-cholesterol acyltransferase (LCAT) and lipoprotein lipase (LPL). These lipid alterations were correlated with tissue injury markers and inflammatory cytokines. The MPLWH group exhibited more severe metabolic disruption, including marked sulfatide (SL) depletion, lower cholesterol and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-c), and extensive rewiring of lipid-cytokine associations. SL depletion in MPLWH correlated with abundances of COPI-mediated retrograde trafficking proteins in exosomes. Transcriptomic profiling of exosome-treated cells provided functional validation: MPLWOH exosomes induced lipid metabolism and repair-associated epithelial programs, while MPLWH exosomes drove phospholipid remodeling and acute inflammatory and mucosal barrier-stress responses. CONCLUSIONS: MPXV infection reprograms host lipid metabolism and exosome composition, with HIV co-infection amplifying inflammatory, metabolic, and trafficking disruptions. These convergent multi-omics signatures link systemic lipid dysregulation to exosome-mediated immunomodulation and identify potential targets for host-directed interventions. FUNDING: This study was funded by the Major Project of Guangzhou National Laboratory.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:猴痘病毒(MPXV)感染多种人类细胞类型,且人类免疫缺陷病毒(HIV)共感染较为常见。MPXV感染的免疫代谢后果以及HIV如何改变这些过程仍不明确。方法:我们在一项发现队列研究(n = 81)中进行了定量血浆脂质组学和精确代谢组学分析,该队列包括MPXV单感染(MPLWOH)、MPXV-HIV共感染(MPLWH)和HIV单感染(PLWH)患者以及健康对照组,并整合了外泌体蛋白组学、细胞因子谱分析以及外泌体处理的HepG2和A549细胞的转录组学数据,以进行功能解释。独立验证队列研究(n = 65)用于评估跨队列研究的可重复性。发现:MPXV感染导致广泛的脂质重塑,表现为磷脂酰丝氨酸(PS)和磷脂酰乙醇胺(PE)升高,而磷脂酰胆碱(PC)、溶血磷脂、胆固醇酯(CE)以及外泌体中的卵磷脂胆固醇乙酰转移酶(LCAT)和脂蛋白脂肪酶(LPL)水平降低。这些脂质变化与组织损伤标志物和炎症细胞因子相关。MPLWH组表现出更严重的代谢紊乱,包括显著的硫酸脑苷脂(SL)减少、胆固醇和高密度脂蛋白胆固醇(HDL-c)水平降低,以及脂质-细胞因子关联的广泛重塑。MPLWH组中SL的减少与外泌体中COPI介导的逆行运输蛋白的丰度相关。外泌体处理细胞的转录组学分析提供了功能验证:MPLWOH外泌体诱导与脂质代谢和修复相关的上皮程序,而MPLWH外泌体则驱动磷脂重塑及急性炎症和黏膜屏障应激反应。结论:MPXV感染重新编程了宿主的脂质代谢和外泌体组成,HIV共感染则放大了炎症、代谢和运输的紊乱。这些一致的多组学特征将系统性脂质失调与外泌体介导的免疫调节联系起来,并指出了针对宿主的潜在干预靶点。资助:本研究由广州国家实验室重大专项资助。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究探讨了猴痘病毒(MPXV)感染的免疫代谢后果,以及人类免疫缺陷病毒(HIV)共感染如何改变这些过程,尽管MPXV具有广泛的细胞嗜性且HIV共感染较为常见,但这些过程此前仍未明确。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究在一项发现队列研究中进行了定量血浆脂质组学和代谢组学分析,该队列包括81名参与者,涵盖MPXV单感染、MPXV-HIV共感染、HIV单感染患者以及健康对照组,并使用独立验证队列研究(n = 65)评估结果的可重复性。
analysis_zh.methods: 进行了血浆脂质组学和代谢组学分析,并结合外泌体蛋白组学、细胞因子谱分析以及外泌体处理的HepG2和A549细胞的转录组学分析,以功能化解释研究结果。
analysis_zh.main_results: MPXV感染导致广泛的脂质重塑,表现为磷脂酰丝氨酸和磷脂酰乙醇胺升高,而磷脂酰胆碱、溶血磷脂、胆固醇酯以及外泌体中的卵磷脂胆固醇乙酰转移酶(LCAT)和脂蛋白脂肪酶(LPL)水平降低,这些变化与组织损伤标志物和炎症细胞因子相关。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,MPXV感染重新编程了宿主的脂质代谢和外泌体组成,HIV共感染则放大了炎症、代谢和运输的紊乱,并识别出将系统性脂质失调与外泌体介导的免疫调节联系起来的一致多组学特征。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明,针对宿主的干预措施可能成为缓解猴痘和猴痘-HIV共感染中免疫代谢失调的潜在靶点,为未来的治疗和诊断策略提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性包括缺乏纵向采样和体内功能验证,这限制了因果推断和结果的普遍性,因此证据的可信度为中等。

papers.title: Monkeypox virus clade IIb isolate exhibits reduced virulence relative to clade IIa isolates in multiple murine models
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Monkeypox virus (MPXV) is the causative agent of mpox disease in humans. The virus comprises two clades, Central African clade I and West African clade II, with case fatality rates of ~11 and ~4%, respectively. Since the discovery of mpox disease in 1970, the virus has been restricted to Africa. However, in 2022, a previously unrecognized subclade IIb caused the largest global outbreak of mpox disease with a case fatality rate of ~0.2%. The difference in virulence of MPXV subclades in human infection warrants further investigation; however, one critical limitation is the lack of susceptible small animal models. In this study, we investigated the susceptibility of four murine models, including CAST-EiJ and three immunocompromised models (C57BL/6 Ifnar −/− , C57BL/6 Ifngr −/− , and C57BL/6 Ifnar −/− / Ifngr −/− ) to MPXV clade IIa (WR 7-61 and US-2003) and IIb (MA-2022) isolates. All four mouse models were susceptible to clade IIa infection, leading to severe disease marked by decreased body temperature, weight loss, and lethality. In contrast, clade IIb infection produced minimal to mild disease at similar doses in all four murine models. The clade IIb isolate produced severe disease (40% lethality) at only the highest dose (8.0 log 10 PFU) in the most susceptible immunocompromised mouse model, C57BL/6 Ifnar −/− / Ifngr −/− . This is the first demonstration of lethal disease with clade IIb in a murine model. In addition, these data show that clade IIa is ~100 to 100,000-fold more virulent than clade IIb and provides three additional murine models for investigating MPXV infection and pathogenesis. IMPORTANCE Mpox is an emerging human disease caused by four distinct MPXV subclades (Ia, Ib, IIa, and IIb). Despite genetic similarities, the case fatality rate varies considerably between the subclades: Ia (~11%), Ib and IIa (~4%), and IIb (~0.2%). Since 2022, multiple mpox outbreaks have occurred due to previously unrecognized subclades, leading to the declaration of two public health emergencies by the World Health Organization. This unprecedented global spread, coupled with the variation in the severity of human disease, underscores the importance of research into the pathogenesis of emerging MPXV subclades. However, a critical limitation is the lack of suitable small animal models. This study identifies three additional murine models susceptible to MPXV clade II infection and demonstrates significant virulence differences between clades IIa and IIb. These models will enable a rapid characterization of previously unrecognized subclades and will facilitate countermeasure development.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Mpox is an emerging human disease caused by distinct Monkeypox virus (MPXV) subclades with widely varying case fatality rates, yet the virulence differences between subclades remain insufficiently understood due to the lack of suitable small animal models.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study evaluated susceptibility of four murine models—CAST-EiJ and three immunocompromised strains (C57BL/6 Ifnar −/− , C57BL/6 Ifngr −/− , and C57BL/6 Ifnar −/− / Ifngr −/− )—to MPXV clade IIa (WR 7-61 and US-2003) and clade IIb (MA-2022) isolates.
analysis.methods: The authors infected mice with standardized doses of clade IIa and IIb isolates and monitored disease progression through clinical signs including body temperature, weight loss, and lethality.
analysis.main_results: All four mouse models developed severe disease after clade IIa infection, whereas clade IIb infection produced minimal to mild disease at similar doses; only the most immunocompromised model (C57BL/6 Ifnar −/− / Ifngr −/− ) showed 40% lethality at the highest clade IIb dose (8.0 log10 PFU).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate clade IIa is approximately 100- to 100,000-fold more virulent than clade IIb in murine models and provide the first lethal clade IIb infection in mice, identifying three new models for MPXV research.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These murine models enable rapid characterization of emerging MPXV subclades and facilitate countermeasure development, addressing a critical gap in mpox research infrastructure.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its exclusive use of murine models, which may not fully recapitulate human disease, and by the absence of data on clade Ib or clade I isolates, reducing generalisability to all MPXV subclades.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated virulence differences between Monkeypox virus (MPXV) clade IIa and clade IIb isolates using four murine models. All models were susceptible to clade IIa infection, resulting in severe disease and lethality, whereas clade IIb infection produced minimal to mild disease at comparable doses. Only the most immunocompromised C57BL/6 Ifnar −/− / Ifngr −/− mice exhibited 40% lethality at the highest clade IIb dose, demonstrating clade IIa is approximately 100- to 100,000-fold more virulent than clade IIb. The work provides the first lethal clade IIb infection in mice and identifies three new murine models for MPXV research, enabling rapid characterization of emerging subclades and countermeasure development.

papers.title: MPOX: ASPECTOS GERAIS E O USO DA ABORDAGEM ONE HEALTH NO CONTEXTO DESSA ZOONOSE VIRAL MPOX: GENERAL ASPECTS AND THE USE OF THE ONE HEALTH APPROACH IN THE CONTEXT OF THIS VIRAL ZOONOSIS MPOX: ASPECTOS GENERALES Y USO DEL ENFOQUE UNA SOLA SALUD EN EL CONTEXTO DE ESTA ZOONOSIS VIRAL
papers.abstract: A Mpox é uma zoonose viral emergente de distribuição global, causada pelo Monkeypox vírus (MPXV), pertencente ao gênero Orthopoxvirus. O presente estudo teve como objetivo descrever de forma breve e pontual as principais características da Mpox e apresentar informações sobre o uso da abordagem One Health como forma de enfrentamento a essa zoonose. Trata-se de uma revisão narrativa da literatura, com seleção de publicações realizadas entre 2014 e 2025, utilizando as bases de dados LILACS, SciELO, PubMed e Google Acadêmico. Além disso, documentos de órgãos oficiais nacionais e internacionais foram pesquisados no contexto do estudo. O MPXV é um vírus de DNA de fita dupla, identificado inicialmente em animais em 1958 e em humanos na década de 1970, apresentando dois clados com potencial para causar infecções. Clinicamente, a Mpox manifesta-se em fases prodrômica e eruptiva, caracterizadas por febre, linfadenopatia e lesões cutâneas. A transmissão ocorre principalmente por contato direto com lesões e secreções, sendo o diagnóstico confirmado por PCR. O manejo da doença inclui cuidados relacionados aos sintomas e tratamento das complicações secundárias. A abordagem One Health, ao integrar ações entre saúde humana, animal e ambiental, torna-se relevante no contexto dessa zoonose. A Mpox apresenta relação com fatores comportamentais e sociais, impactando grupos específicos, necessitando de medidas de prevenção e políticas públicas efetivas. A cooperação interdisciplinar e o fortalecimento da vigilância epidemiológica são fundamentais para o controle efetivo da Mpox a partir da abordagem One Health.

analysis.summary_en: This study provides an overview of the Mpox virus, highlighting its status as a globally emerging viral zoonosis caused by MPXV, a member of the Orthopoxvirus genus. The research aims to briefly describe the main characteristics of Mpox and emphasize the importance of the One Health approach in addressing this zoonosis. The study is a narrative literature review of publications from 2014 to 2025, sourced from databases such as LILACS, SciELO, PubMed, and Google Scholar, along with official documents. It outlines that transmission occurs primarily through direct contact with lesions and secretions, and diagnosis is confirmed via PCR. Clinically, Mpox presents in prodromic and eruptive phases, marked by fever, lymphadenopathy, and skin lesions. The findings suggest that Mpox is linked to behavioral and social factors, affecting specific groups and requiring effective prevention measures and public policies. The One Health approach is deemed essential for managing the disease by integrating human, animal, and environmental health actions. The study acknowledges the need for interdisciplinary cooperation and strengthened epidemiological surveillance for effective control. However, it does not provide detailed statistical or methodological limitations, which may affect the strength of the evidence.

papers.title_zh: 猴痘:猴痘的一般特征及在该人兽共患病毒病背景下的“同一健康”方法应用
papers.source_body_en: A Mpox é uma zoonose viral emergente de distribuição global, causada pelo Monkeypox vírus (MPXV), pertencente ao gênero Orthopoxvirus. O presente estudo teve como objetivo descrever de forma breve e pontual as principais características da Mpox e apresentar informações sobre o uso da abordagem One Health como forma de enfrentamento a essa zoonose. Trata-se de uma revisão narrativa da literatura, com seleção de publicações realizadas entre 2014 e 2025, utilizando as bases de dados LILACS, SciELO, PubMed e Google Acadêmico. Além disso, documentos de órgãos oficiais nacionais e internacionais foram pesquisados no contexto do estudo. O MPXV é um vírus de DNA de fita dupla, identificado inicialmente em animais em 1958 e em humanos na década de 1970, apresentando dois clados com potencial para causar infecções. Clinicamente, a Mpox manifesta-se em fases prodrômica e eruptiva, caracterizadas por febre, linfadenopatia e lesões cutâneas. A transmissão ocorre principalmente por contato direto com lesões e secreções, sendo o diagnóstico confirmado por PCR. O manejo da doença inclui cuidados relacionados aos sintomas e tratamento das complicações secundárias. A abordagem One Health, ao integrar ações entre saúde humana, animal e ambiental, torna-se relevante no contexto dessa zoonose. A Mpox apresenta relação com fatores comportamentais e sociais, impactando grupos específicos, necessitando de medidas de prevenção e políticas públicas efetivas. A cooperação interdisciplinar e o fortalecimento da vigilância epidemiológica são fundamentais para o controle efetivo da Mpox a partir da abordagem One Health.

papers.title: Enhancing Interpretability for Automated Human Monkeypox Skin Lesions Detection Using Pre-trained Transfer Learning Networks
papers.abstract: Abstract Identification of skin lesions remains a challenging task because of low image contrast, large variations in disease manifestations, and strong visual similarities among dermatological conditions. Deep transfer learning (TL)-integrated artificial intelligence (AI) systems offer an effective solution for rapid and accurate computer-aided diagnosis of multiple infectious skin diseases. In this study, a TL-based framework is proposed as an automated human monkeypox (MP) skin lesion detection (HMSLD) for monkeypox (MP), chickenpox (CP), measles (MS), and normal skin lesion classification. A publicly available dataset comprising 654 RGB clinical images. The HMSLD performed image preprocessing, data augmentation, class imbalance handling through inverse class weighting, and comparative analysis of pre-trained TL models, namely Xception, ResNet152V2, NASNetLarge, EfficientNetB0, EfficientNetB7, MobileNetV2, and MobileNetV3. MobileNetV3 performed best among the models. Their overall performance with an accuracy = 91%, precision = 91%, recall = 89%, F1-score = 90%, and an AUROC of 0.99, indicating excellent discriminative capability. MobileNetV3 achieved 96% precision for measles and 100% recall for normal skin, while EfficientNetB0 performed the highest precision at 96% and an F1-score of 93%. MobileNetV3 provides the most balanced trade-off among the evaluated models between classification accuracy, robustness, and computational efficiency. These evaluated performances indicate the potential of the HMSLD framework. It may be a reliable and cost-effective computer-aided diagnostic tool for early MP screening and other clinically similar skin diseases.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, India Section A: Physical Sciences

papers.title_zh: 利用预训练迁移学习网络提升自动化人类猴痘皮肤病变检测的可解释性
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Identification of skin lesions remains a challenging task because of low image contrast, large variations in disease manifestations, and strong visual similarities among dermatological conditions. Deep transfer learning (TL)-integrated artificial intelligence (AI) systems offer an effective solution for rapid and accurate computer-aided diagnosis of multiple infectious skin diseases. In this study, a TL-based framework is proposed as an automated human monkeypox (MP) skin lesion detection (HMSLD) for monkeypox (MP), chickenpox (CP), measles (MS), and normal skin lesion classification. A publicly available dataset comprising 654 RGB clinical images. The HMSLD performed image preprocessing, data augmentation, class imbalance handling through inverse class weighting, and comparative analysis of pre-trained TL models, namely Xception, ResNet152V2, NASNetLarge, EfficientNetB0, EfficientNetB7, MobileNetV2, and MobileNetV3. MobileNetV3 performed best among the models. Their overall performance with an accuracy = 91%, precision = 91%, recall = 89%, F1-score = 90%, and an AUROC of 0.99, indicating excellent discriminative capability. MobileNetV3 achieved 96% precision for measles and 100% recall for normal skin, while EfficientNetB0 performed the highest precision at 96% and an F1-score of 93%. MobileNetV3 provides the most balanced trade-off among the evaluated models between classification accuracy, robustness, and computational efficiency. These evaluated performances indicate the potential of the HMSLD framework. It may be a reliable and cost-effective computer-aided diagnostic tool for early MP screening and other clinically similar skin diseases.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 由于图像对比度低、疾病表现变异大以及皮肤病变在视觉上的高度相似性,皮肤病变识别仍是一项具有挑战性的任务。深度迁移学习(TL)集成人工智能(AI)系统为多种传染性皮肤病的快速准确计算机辅助诊断提供了有效解决方案。本研究提出了一种基于TL的框架,用于自动化人类猴痘(MP)皮肤病变检测(HMSLD),以对猴痘(MP)、水痘(CP)、麻疹(MS)及正常皮肤病变进行分类。该研究使用了一个公开可用的数据集,包含654张RGB临床图像。HMSLD框架进行了图像预处理、数据增强、通过逆类权重处理类别不平衡,并对预训练TL模型(包括Xception、ResNet152V2、NASNetLarge、EfficientNetB0、EfficientNetB7、MobileNetV2和MobileNetV3)进行了比较分析。MobileNetV3在所有模型中表现最佳。其整体性能为:准确率=91%,精确率=91%,召回率=89%,F1值=90%,AUROC为0.99,表明具有优异的判别能力。MobileNetV3在麻疹检测中实现了96%的精确率,在正常皮肤检测中实现了100%的召回率,而EfficientNetB0在精确率上表现最佳(96%)且F1值为93%。MobileNetV3在所评估模型中提供了分类准确性、鲁棒性与计算效率之间最为平衡的权衡。这些评估性能表明HMSLD框架具有潜在应用价值,可能成为一种可靠且具有成本效益的计算机辅助诊断工具,用于早期猴痘筛查及其他临床相似皮肤疾病。

papers.full_text: Presentation Type: Poster Presentation Subject Category: Surveillance Abstract ID: 196 Breakthrough COVID-19 Infections Among Vaccinated Residents of VA Community Living Centers Brandon Smith1 EST Healthcare water management programs (WMPs) have historically emphasized the control of Legionella pneumophila, largely due to its estab- lished role in Legionnaires’ disease outbreaks. However, healthcare water systems harbor a wide range of opportunistic premise plumbing pathogens (OPPPs), including nontuberculous mycobacteria (NTM), Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Acinetobacter baumannii, Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, and Burkholderia cepacia complex. These organisms exhibit distinct eco- logical preferences and persistence mechanisms that vary by system type. In this study, we analyze microbiological testing data from more than 200,000 healthcare-associated water system samples collected since September 2019, comparing pathogen positivity across ice machines, gen- eral potable water, and cooling towers. Results demonstrate substantial variability in pathogen positivity by system type, with NTM showing mark- edly higher positivity in ice machines and potable water systems (relative to traditional indicator organisms). Legionella pneumophila positivity was highest in cooling towers but substantially lower in potable water. These findings indicate that uniform, organism-agnostic surveillance strategies are insufficient and that WMPs must be selectively designed based on sys- tem type, exposure route, and patient risk. Adopting site-specific, organ- ism-selective monitoring frameworks may significantly improve infection prevention efforts in healthcare settings. Antimicrobial Stewardship & Healthcare Epidemiology 2026;6(Suppl. S1):s185 doi:10.1017/ash.2026.10727 Presentation Type: Poster Presentation Subject Category: Surveillance Abstract ID: 226 Patterns and Gaps in Mpox Vaccination at NYC Health + Hospitals, a Large Urban Safety Net Health System in New York City, 2022-2025 Shatha AlShanqeeti1, Gaayathri Krishnan2, Crisanta Simon, Jonathan Baghdadi1, Katherine Goodman1, Gregory Schrank1, Jessica Holman, Lisa Pineles3, Cassie Cunningham Goedken4, Christine Firestone, KC Coffey5, Westyn Branch-Elliman, Surbhi Leekha6, Anthony Harris1 and Daniel Morgan1 1University of Maryland School of Medicine; 2University of Maryland; 3University of Maryland, Baltimore; 4Center for Access & Delivery Research & Evaluation (CADRE), Iowa City Veterans Affairs Health Care System, Iowa City, IA, USA; 5Massachusetts General Hospital and 6University of Maryland Baltimore Background: Hospital onset bacteremia and fungemia (HOB) is under development as a Center for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) auto- mated digital quality measure. We evaluated the use of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in assessing attribution and preventability of HOB. Methods This is a retrospective cohort study of hospitalized patients with positive blood cultures at 11 US Veterans Affairs (VA) hospitals. We included a random sample of positive blood cultures collected after day 3 of admission where admission date is day 1. GenAI (OpenAI GPT- 4o) was prompted to provide the most likely source and adjudicate the pre- ventability of HOB using standardized prompts and clinical data (GenAI). IP experts used GenAI output to provide GenAI-assisted determinations of source and preventability of HOB (IP-AI). HOB event preventability was rated by IP expert using a 6-point Likert scale, responses were combined to 3 categories for analysis. We compared initial GenAI with IP-AI determi- nations of source and preventability. A separate human-only review by a different IP expert was performed (IP-alone) on a random subset to com- pare time required for review. Results We included 52 HOB events for IP- AI and a subset of 21 for IP-alone. Enterobacterales were the most common organisms (22/52, 42%) followed by Staphylococcus aureus (9/52, 17%). Median duration to HOB event was 12 (IQR 5 – 31) days. GenAI most commonly attributed bacteremia to gastrointestinal (GI) (14/52, 26.9%), followed by genitourinary (GU) (12/52, 23%), central line (CLABSI) (8/ 52, 15%), and skin and soft tissue infections (SSTI) (7/52, 14%) sources (Figure 1). IP-AI determination of source agreed with GenAI source in 67% (35/52) of cases. Most agreement between IP-AI and GenAI occurred when HOB was attributed to a bone and joint infection (2/2, 100%), fol- lowed by GI source (13/14, 93%), SSTI (5/7, 71%), and GU source (7/12, 58%). Most disagreements (17/52, 33%) occurred when IP-AI attribution was to an unknown source (5/17, 29%) or blood culture contamination (3/ 17, 18%). GenAI adjudication of preventability matched IP-AI adjudica- tion in 20/52 (39%). The median time to complete an IP-AI review was 11.5 (IQR 6 – 20.5) minutes compared to a median of 25 (IQR 13 – 33) minutes for IP-alone. Conclusion IP experts often agreed with GenAI for source of HOB but disagreed with its preventability. GenAI rarely acknowledged unknown source. Using GenAI for HOB detection is faster than human review but must account for differences in preventability. Antimicrobial Stewardship & Healthcare Epidemiology 2026;6(Suppl. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the use of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in assessing the attribution and preventability of hospital-onset bacteremia and fungemia (HOB) events.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This is a retrospective cohort study of hospitalized patients with positive blood cultures at 11 US Veterans Affairs (VA) hospitals, including a random sample of positive blood cultures collected after day 3 of admission.
analysis.methods: GenAI (OpenAI GPT-4o) was prompted to provide the most likely source and adjudicate the preventability of HOB using standardized prompts and clinical data. IP experts used GenAI output to provide GenAI-assisted determinations of source and preventability, and a separate human-only review by a different IP expert was performed on a random subset.
analysis.main_results: GenAI most commonly attributed bacteremia to gastrointestinal (GI) sources (14/52, 26.9%), followed by genitourinary (GU) (12/52, 23%), central line (CLABSI) (8/52, 15%), and skin and soft tissue infections (SSTI) (7/52, 14%) sources. IP-AI determination of source agreed with GenAI source in 67% (35/52) of cases, while GenAI adjudication of preventability matched IP-AI adjudication in 20/52 (39%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that IP experts often agreed with GenAI for the source of HOB but disagreed with its preventability, indicating that while GenAI can assist in identifying sources, it may not be reliable for assessing preventability.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that integrating GenAI into HOB surveillance could enhance the speed of source identification but must be complemented by expert judgment for preventability assessments, which is critical for infection prevention strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on GenAI for preventability adjudication, which may not align with expert opinions, and the small sample size of HOB events analyzed. The evidence is moderate due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the use of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in assessing the attribution and preventability of hospital-onset bacteremia and fungemia (HOB) events. A retrospective cohort study was conducted on hospitalized patients with positive blood cultures at 11 US Veterans Affairs (VA) hospitals, focusing on HOB events occurring after day 3 of admission. GenAI was used to identify potential sources of HOB, and IP experts provided GenAI-assisted determinations. The results showed that GenAI attributed HOB events to gastrointestinal sources most frequently, with IP-AI agreeing with GenAI in 67% of cases. However, GenAI's preventability assessments matched IP-AI only in 39% of cases. The study highlights that while GenAI can expedite source identification, its role in preventability assessments requires expert validation. The findings suggest that integrating GenAI into HOB surveillance could improve efficiency but must be paired with human expertise for accurate preventability judgments. The evidence is moderate due to the limitations in GenAI's preventability adjudication and the relatively small sample size.

papers.title: Finger-actuated microfluidic device for point-of-care circulating cell-free nucleic acid extraction.
papers.abstract: Timely and accurate nucleic acid extraction is a critical bottleneck in point-of-care (POC) molecular diagnostics, particularly for low-abundance cell-free nucleic acids (DNA, RNA, miRNA) in plasma. We present a fully finger-actuated microfluidic device for power-free, pipette-free, nucleic acid extraction. The prototype device integrates finger-actuated valves, pump and blister reagent storage, enabling a complete, intuitive, "sample-to-eluate" workflow, including lysis, binding, washing and elution via manual actuation in approximately 35 minutes. The device operation was benchmarked against a commercial magnetic bead-based manual benchtop and an automated robotic workflow. In DNA-spiked aqueous samples (5-20 ng mL -1 ), the device demonstrated recoveries of 84.6%, against 90.7% on the bench. Optimisation of magnetic bead volume identified 50 μL as the threshold for maximal recovery while minimising reagent consumption. Recovery from human pooled plasma samples were found to be on average 18, 62, and 552% higher than that obtained with the control bench extraction on initial sample volumes of 100, 75 and 50 μL, respectively. Coefficient of variation (CV%) for all techniques remained within reported laboratory ranges (20-80%). The device's clinical utility was piloted using patient samples positive for cytomegalovirus (CMV), monkeypox virus (MPXV) or chikungunya (CHIKV). The device achieved successful qPCR amplification for all targets, with viral DNA Cq values within as little as 0.3 cycles of the standard protocol. This instrument-free, manual circulating nucleic acid extraction tool could help bridge the gap between lateral flow based nucleic acid amplification technologies and real-world decentralised diagnostics, offering a scalable solution for infectious disease management in resource-limited settings.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the critical need for rapid, accessible nucleic acid extraction at the point of care to enable decentralised molecular diagnostics, particularly for low-abundance circulating cell-free nucleic acids in clinical samples.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The authors developed and evaluated a finger-actuated microfluidic device designed for power-free, pipette-free nucleic acid extraction with a manual, instrument-free workflow.
analysis.methods: The device integrates finger-actuated valves, a pump, and blister-based reagent storage to perform lysis, binding, washing, and elution in approximately 35 minutes, and was benchmarked against commercial magnetic bead-based manual and automated robotic workflows.
analysis.main_results: In DNA-spiked aqueous samples (5–20 ng mL−1), the device achieved 84.6% recovery compared to 90.7% for the bench control, while in human pooled plasma, recoveries were 18%, 62%, and 552% higher than the bench extraction at initial volumes of 100, 75, and 50 μL, respectively.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the device as enabling a scalable, decentralised solution for nucleic acid extraction that maintains performance close to standard protocols, with clinical utility demonstrated by successful qPCR amplification from patient samples positive for cytomegalovirus, monkeypox virus, or chikungunya.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The device could bridge the gap between lateral flow nucleic acid amplification technologies and decentralised diagnostics, supporting infectious disease management in resource-limited settings where infrastructure and power are constrained.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to proof-of-concept and pilot testing with small sample sizes and abstract-level data, indicating moderate strength and the need for larger, controlled clinical evaluations to confirm performance and generalisability.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces a finger-actuated microfluidic device designed to enable power-free, pipette-free nucleic acid extraction for point-of-care diagnostics. The device integrates manual actuation for lysis, binding, washing, and elution in a 35-minute workflow and was benchmarked against commercial magnetic bead-based methods. In DNA-spiked samples, recovery was 84.6% versus 90.7% for the bench control, while in plasma, recoveries exceeded bench extraction by 18% to 552% depending on sample volume. Pilot testing with patient samples positive for cytomegalovirus, monkeypox virus, or chikungunya demonstrated successful qPCR amplification with cycle quantification values within 0.3 cycles of standard protocols. The authors propose the device as a scalable solution for decentralised diagnostics in resource-limited settings, though current evidence is limited to small-scale, abstract-level evaluations and requires further validation.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the critical need for rapid, accessible nucleic acid extraction at the point of care to enable decentralised molecular diagnostics, particularly for low-abundance circulating cell-free nucleic acids in clinical samples.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The authors developed and evaluated a finger-actuated microfluidic device designed for power-free, pipette-free nucleic acid extraction with a manual, instrument-free workflow.
analysis_en.methods: The device integrates finger-actuated valves, a pump, and blister-based reagent storage to perform lysis, binding, washing, and elution in approximately 35 minutes, and was benchmarked against commercial magnetic bead-based manual and automated robotic workflows.
analysis_en.main_results: In DNA-spiked aqueous samples (5–20 ng mL−1), the device achieved 84.6% recovery compared to 90.7% for the bench control, while in human pooled plasma, recoveries were 18%, 62%, and 552% higher than the bench extraction at initial volumes of 100, 75, and 50 μL, respectively.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the device as enabling a scalable, decentralised solution for nucleic acid extraction that maintains performance close to standard protocols, with clinical utility demonstrated by successful qPCR amplification from patient samples positive for cytomegalovirus, monkeypox virus, or chikungunya.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The device could bridge the gap between lateral flow nucleic acid amplification technologies and decentralised diagnostics, supporting infectious disease management in resource-limited settings where infrastructure and power are constrained.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to proof-of-concept and pilot testing with small sample sizes and abstract-level data, indicating moderate strength and the need for larger, controlled clinical evaluations to confirm performance and generalisability.

papers.title_zh: 指动式微流控设备用于即时检测循环无细胞核酸提取
papers.source_body_en: Timely and accurate nucleic acid extraction is a critical bottleneck in point-of-care (POC) molecular diagnostics, particularly for low-abundance cell-free nucleic acids (DNA, RNA, miRNA) in plasma. We present a fully finger-actuated microfluidic device for power-free, pipette-free, nucleic acid extraction. The prototype device integrates finger-actuated valves, pump and blister reagent storage, enabling a complete, intuitive, "sample-to-eluate" workflow, including lysis, binding, washing and elution via manual actuation in approximately 35 minutes. The device operation was benchmarked against a commercial magnetic bead-based manual benchtop and an automated robotic workflow. In DNA-spiked aqueous samples (5-20 ng mL -1 ), the device demonstrated recoveries of 84.6%, against 90.7% on the bench. Optimisation of magnetic bead volume identified 50 μL as the threshold for maximal recovery while minimising reagent consumption. Recovery from human pooled plasma samples were found to be on average 18, 62, and 552% higher than that obtained with the control bench extraction on initial sample volumes of 100, 75 and 50 μL, respectively. Coefficient of variation (CV%) for all techniques remained within reported laboratory ranges (20-80%). The device's clinical utility was piloted using patient samples positive for cytomegalovirus (CMV), monkeypox virus (MPXV) or chikungunya (CHIKV). The device achieved successful qPCR amplification for all targets, with viral DNA Cq values within as little as 0.3 cycles of the standard protocol. This instrument-free, manual circulating nucleic acid extraction tool could help bridge the gap between lateral flow based nucleic acid amplification technologies and real-world decentralised diagnostics, offering a scalable solution for infectious disease management in resource-limited settings.
